metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Limited to 'improved auto-completion' or mechanical/repeated tasks; vibe-coded contributions banned; any LLM usage must be disclosed via ticket label, comment, or commit message.
domains.accountability_wording: The contributing human author is ultimately responsible for every line of code, comment, or mailing list interaction they initiate

evidence.quote: Human contributors must be the primary author(s) of GDAL contributions
LLMs may only be used as an improved auto-completion mechanism, or for repeated tasks (mechanical refactoring)
Any LLM usage must be indicated by ticket label, comment, or commit message indication and account for what was written by whom/what.
The contributing human author is ultimately responsible for every line of code, comment, or mailing list interaction they initiate

domains.reasoning: Explicitly names code, ticket comments, and commit messages as the scope; states a mix of human-in-the-loop and disclosure requirements, bans vibe-coding, and assigns accountability to the contributing human author. Meets 'yes' threshold.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no accountability holder; no scope stated
domains.reasoning: The policy makes no mention of meeting recording, transcription, or notetaker bots of any kind.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level for docs/blogs/design assets; no accountability holder
domains.reasoning: The policy scopes itself to code, ticket comments, commit messages, and mailing list interaction. It does not name documentation, blog posts, or design assets, so content is not addressed even though 'contributions' is used generically elsewhere.

domains.rationale_only_mention: Indiscriminate usage of LLMs in open source projects *consume* maintenance, and the GDAL LLM tool policy attempts to conserve that resource.
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI-assisted moderation; no supervision level or accountability holder
domains.reasoning: The 'maintainer time as constrained resource' language is rationale for the overall contribution restrictions, not a rule about whether maintainers may use AI to take moderation actions. The clause about locking/closing/banning non-compliant contributors is enforcement of the AI policy itself, not a statement about AI-assisted moderation, so it does not supply an accountability holder for this domain.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI-assisted review; no supervision level or accountability holder
domains.reasoning: The document discusses review as a scarce maintainer resource but never states whether maintainers or reviewers may themselves use AI tools to review contributions.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Banned specifically for submission of contributions to the GDAL repository, whether human-coordinated or fully autonomous (e.g. OpenClaw-style agents).

evidence.quote: Human-coordinated or uncoordinated (OpenClaw, etc) use of agents for submission of contributions to the GDAL repository is *banned*.

domains.reasoning: Names agentic/autonomous submission specifically and sets a clear supervision level (banned). No accountability holder is assigned for this banned activity, but the domain is otherwise substantively addressed with a named scope.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of energy/water/carbon impact; no rule stated
domains.reasoning: The rationale section discusses maintenance burden and copyright uncertainty as reasons for the policy, but never raises energy, water, or carbon footprint concerns.

domains.rationale_only_mention: The GDAL sponsorship_program is one way your organization can help buffer the cost and disruption of LLMs in keystone projects such as GDAL.
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on server load or hardware financing; no supervision level stated
domains.reasoning: The Mitigation section frames sponsorship as a way to offset the financial 'cost and disruption' LLMs bring to the project, but this is offered as a funding suggestion, not a rule with a supervision level or accountability holder for infrastructure strain.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on GDAL's own content/data being used to train models
domains.reasoning: The rationale mentions uncertainty over whether LLM output is a derived work of its training data (a copyright/provenance concern about code contributions), but this is not a statement about GDAL's own issues, discussions, or user data being used to train external models, so the training_data domain as defined is not addressed.

unscoped_statements.quote: Contributors can make **limited use** of LLMs for contributions in GDAL, subject to details mentioned below

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: GDAL's policy is detailed and restrictive specifically for code/ticket/commit contributions (human-in-the-loop, disclosure required, vibe-coding and agentic submission banned, contributor held accountable) and separately bans autonomous agentic submission, but it is silent on notetaker bots, documentation/content, AI-assisted review, AI-assisted moderation, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and use of the project's own data for training - maintenance burden and LLM cost are cited only as rationale, not governed by any stated rule.

validation_problems: code_contributions: quote not found in doc/source/community/ai_tool_policy.rst

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
